case_title: ISSAC @ KISHOR v. RONALD CHERIYAN AND ORS.
high_court_outcome: remitted the matter back to the trial court for re-trial
neutral_facts: The deceased, a widow, lived alone in her house, which was part of five acres of agricultural land. The accused no.1, who was working as a domestic help, started staying with the deceased after her employer, Natarajan, was directed to leave. On the night of the incident, the deceased's sister-in-law heard cries from the house and alerted her son, who then went to the house. The accused no.1 was found tied with a rope in the kitchen, while the deceased was found unconscious in the front room. The accused no.1 claimed that five thieves had entered the house, suffocated the deceased, and took valuables. The police registered a case against five persons, and the accused no.2 was arrested based on a disclosure statement. Evidence included fingerprints, recovered items, and a post-mortem report indicating suffocation as the cause of death. The trial court acquitted the accused no.1, citing insufficient evidence, while convicting the accused no.2. The High Court remitted the matter for re-trial due to procedural irregularities.
